problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=6t+6{t}^{2},$ where $t>0$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=2$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t.$

feedback.problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with velocity $v(t)=3{t}^{2}-2,$ where $t$ is the time. If the particle is at the position $x=-1$ when $t=0,$ calculate the position $x$ of the particle at time $t>0.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We start by integrating the velocity to get $x(t):$

$$
\begin{aligned}x(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int (3{t}^{2}-2)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={t}^{3}-2t+C\end{aligned}
$$

To determine $C,$ we use the fact that $x(0)=-1.$ Substituting this into the above gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1 & =(0)^{3}-2(0)+C \\ C & =-1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the position $x$ of the particle at time $t$ is

$$
x(t)={t}^{3}-2t-1.
$$
